paragraphs: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yitzchak. (A tanna cited in a baraita.)

In Kiddushin 54a, the baraita reads: “R. Y. son of R. Y. said: The stones of Jerusalem that fell are subject to me’ilah—the words of Rabbi Meir,” etc. Without doubt this is a copyist’s error, and it should read: “Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yitzchak recited the teaching.” In fact, he was an amora, a student of Rabbi Yochanan. In Yoma, chapter 3, halakhah 7: “R' Yishmael son of Rav Yitzchak; Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai.”[^1][^2]

notes.text: The first attribution is printed אר״י בר״י. Its initials are not expanded into a new full patronymic; the earlier English “Yochanan ben Beroka” had no support in the supplied text. Hyman himself proposes changing the wording to דתני ר׳ ישמעאל בר ר׳ יצחק, treating him as a transmitter of the teaching rather than establishing him as its tanna. The parenthetic tanna label and the subsequent correction are both preserved, as is Hyman’s confidence (“without doubt”). The heading abbreviates Yitzchak’s title as ר׳, while the final citation spells רב יצחק. The Rabbi expansion in the heading is supported by the matching Kiddushin baraita’s explicit רבי יצחק. Me’ilah is the misuse of consecrated property. ר״מ and רש״בי are rendered by their customary names, Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai, without an authority identification. The abbreviated final citation is not expanded into a newly specified chain of transmission. The earlier translation did not independently check either citation or Hyman’s emendation; the subsequent title-only check is recorded below.

In the William Davidson edition, Kiddushin 54a explicitly titles Yishmael, his father Yitzchak, and Meir as Rabbi. The Guggenheimer edition of Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 3:7:4 explicitly titles Yochanan and Shimon ben Yoḥai as Rabbi and the patronymic Yitzchak as Rav, but names the first transmitter Shmuel rather than Hyman’s Yishmael. Hyman’s name is retained here as R' Yishmael, leaving its abbreviated title unresolved. This title check does not establish Hyman’s proposed emendation or resolve the difference in names.
